slots.practicalActivity: On a local SQL Server instance, query sys.dm_os_sys_info and sys.dm_exec_requests to connect the relational-engine and storage-engine concepts to real metadata, then query sys.dm_os_memory_clerks to see how the buffer pool and plan cache are actually consuming memory on your instance right now.
slots.deliverable: A short write-up naming the top 3 memory clerks by memory_used_kb and one sentence connecting each to a concept covered in the lesson (buffer pool, plan cache, or another clerk).

slots.practicalActivity: Run SELECT @@VERSION and SERVERPROPERTY('Edition') to identify your exact edition and build, query sys.dm_os_schedulers to see SQLOS's scheduler-per-core model in action, then query sys.databases filtered to database_id <= 4 to review master, tempdb, model, and msdb's individual recovery models and file locations.
slots.deliverable: A one-page instance profile: edition/version, scheduler count from sys.dm_os_schedulers, and the file paths/recovery models of all four system databases.

slots.practicalActivity: Plan a hypothetical installation on paper first (service accounts, collation, file paths for data/log/tempdb, memory limits), then either perform a real SQL Server Developer Edition install on a VM or local machine, or walk through the setup wizard screen by screen noting every decision point, and finish with the standard post-install checklist: max server memory, backup directory, and error log location.
slots.deliverable: A completed installation-planning checklist covering service accounts, collation choice, file layout, and the 3 post-install settings configured, with the actual chosen values.

slots.practicalActivity: Use sp_configure to review and then adjust at least 3 server-level settings (for example max server memory, cost threshold for parallelism, and max degree of parallelism) on a test instance, documenting the before and after value and the reasoning for each change.
slots.deliverable: A configuration-change log listing each sp_configure setting touched, its before/after value, and a one-sentence justification.

slots.practicalActivity: Query sys.fn_helpcollations() to explore available collations, run SERVERPROPERTY('Collation') and DATABASEPROPERTYEX('AdventureWorks2012','Collation') to compare server vs. database collation, then open SQL Server Configuration Manager to inspect which service account runs the Database Engine and Agent services and what startup parameters are set.
slots.deliverable: A short comparison noting the server's collation, AdventureWorks2012's collation, and a written note of the service accounts shown in Configuration Manager.

slots.practicalActivity: Perform a complete clean install-and-configure pass on a test instance from scratch: install, set collation deliberately, configure max server memory and MAXDOP, verify service accounts in Configuration Manager, and confirm the instance comes up healthy with a SELECT @@SERVERNAME sanity check.
slots.deliverable: A written install runbook documenting every step taken, plus the final sp_configure output proving the memory/MAXDOP settings took effect.

slots.practicalActivity: Use CREATE DATABASE to build a new test database with explicit primary and secondary filegroups and separate data/log files on different logical paths, query sys.database_files and sys.filegroups to confirm the layout, then set at least 3 database options (for example AUTO_CLOSE OFF, PAGE_VERIFY CHECKSUM, READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON) with ALTER DATABASE.
slots.deliverable: The full CREATE DATABASE script with filegroups, the sys.database_files/sys.filegroups output, and a list of the 3 database options set and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Switch the test database between SIMPLE, FULL, and BULK_LOGGED recovery models with ALTER DATABASE, noting what happens to the transaction log at each switch, then query and modify at least 2 database-scoped configuration values (for example MAXDOP and LEGACY_CARDINALITY_ESTIMATION) with ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION.
slots.deliverable: A short write-up of the recovery model chosen and why, plus the database-scoped configuration values changed and their before/after state.

slots.practicalActivity: Review and deliberately set AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS, AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS, and AUTO_SHRINK on the test database (turning AUTO_SHRINK OFF with a justification), then use sp_addextendedproperty to attach a custom extended property (for example an Owner or Environment tag) to the database and confirm it with sys.extended_properties.
slots.deliverable: The ALTER DATABASE statements for the three AUTO settings plus the extended-property script and its sys.extended_properties confirmation output.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a brand-new database end to end to a given spec: named filegroups, a chosen recovery model, database-scoped configuration tuned, AUTO settings set deliberately, and an extended property documenting its purpose — then write a one-paragraph justification of every choice as if handing it off to another DBA.
slots.deliverable: A complete database-setup.sql script plus a short justification write-up covering every configuration decision made.

slots.practicalActivity: Query sys.database_files across all databases to inventory current file sizes, growth settings, and locations, then reconfigure tempdb to use multiple equally-sized data files (one per logical core, up to 8) with ALTER DATABASE tempdb MODIFY FILE, and change autogrowth on one file from percentage-based to a fixed MB increment.
slots.deliverable: A tempdb-configuration script adding the additional data files, plus a before/after sys.database_files comparison showing the new file count and growth settings.

slots.practicalActivity: Document a recommended disk layout for a new production instance (separate volumes for OS, data files, log files, tempdb, and backups), then compare it against the actual current layout of the test instance using sys.master_files joined to sys.dm_os_volume_stats, flagging any volume where data and log files are mixed.
slots.deliverable: A disk-layout table (recommended vs. actual) plus the sys.master_files/sys.dm_os_volume_stats query used to check the actual layout.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine Chapter 4 into a storage health-check script: current file sizes and growth settings for every database, tempdb file count and sizing, and a volume-mixing check flagging any disk holding both data and log files.
slots.deliverable: A saved storage-health-check.sql file with three labeled sections that runs clean against the local instance.

slots.practicalActivity: Confirm the instance's authentication mode with SERVERPROPERTY('IsIntegratedSecurityOnly'), create one Windows-authenticated login and one SQL-authenticated login with CREATE LOGIN, map each to a database user in a test database with CREATE USER ... FOR LOGIN, and query sys.server_principals and sys.database_principals to confirm both exist end to end.
slots.deliverable: The CREATE LOGIN/CREATE USER scripts for both principals plus the sys.server_principals/sys.database_principals query output confirming the mapping.

slots.practicalActivity: Add one of the users from the previous slot to the db_datareader fixed role, then create a custom database role with CREATE ROLE granting SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on exactly 2 named tables (not the whole schema), add the other user to it, and query sys.database_role_members to confirm both memberships.
slots.deliverable: The CREATE ROLE and GRANT statements for the custom role plus a sys.database_role_members query showing both users' role memberships.

slots.practicalActivity: Walk through the setup shape for Transparent Data Encryption on a test database (master key, certificate, database encryption key, ALTER DATABASE SET ENCRYPTION ON) and confirm it with sys.dm_database_encryption_keys, then create a Server Audit and a Server Audit Specification capturing failed logins and trigger one deliberately to confirm it's captured.
slots.deliverable: The TDE setup script plus its sys.dm_database_encryption_keys confirmation, and the audit setup script plus a captured failed-login audit record.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a complete security baseline for a new database: authentication confirmed, at least 2 logins/users created and mapped correctly, a custom role scoped to only the tables it needs, TDE enabled, and an audit specification watching for failed logins and schema changes, documented as a security runbook.
slots.deliverable: A security-baseline.sql script covering logins/users/roles/TDE/audit, plus a one-page security runbook summarizing what's protected and how.

slots.practicalActivity: Use the Maintenance Plan Wizard (or script the equivalent manually) to build a plan that rebuilds/reorganizes indexes based on a fragmentation threshold and updates statistics afterward on a test database, scheduling it as an Agent job, then run it once manually and confirm it completed via the maintenance plan's log.
slots.deliverable: An exported definition of the maintenance plan plus its first successful execution log entry.

lessons.title: Ola Hallengren's Maintenance Scripts, the Industry Standard

slots.practicalActivity: Add a backup step and a DBCC CHECKDB integrity-check step to the maintenance plan from the previous slot, then download and install Ola Hallengren's Maintenance Solution (ola.hallengren.com) into a DBA database on the same test instance, and compare: run his IndexOptimize and DatabaseIntegrityCheck procedures once and note how they differ from the hand-built plan's behavior.
slots.deliverable: A short comparison write-up naming at least 2 concrete advantages Ola Hallengren's solution has over the hand-built maintenance plan, backed by what was observed running both.

slots.practicalActivity: Fully replace the hand-built maintenance plan with Ola Hallengren's solution as the standing maintenance system: install it, wire DatabaseBackup, IndexOptimize, and DatabaseIntegrityCheck into Agent jobs with real schedules, run each once, and confirm success in the CommandLog table it creates.
slots.deliverable: The installed Agent jobs (names/schedules) plus a CommandLog query showing a successful run of each of the three procedures.

slots.practicalActivity: Review how the SQL Server Agent service, msdb, and the job/step/schedule tables relate, then create a new Agent job with at least 2 steps (for example a T-SQL step and a step calling a stored procedure) and attach a recurring schedule, confirming it in the Agent tree in SSMS and in msdb.dbo.sysjobs.
slots.deliverable: The job-creation script (or the wizard-built job's exported definition) plus a msdb.dbo.sysjobs/sysjobsteps query confirming both steps and the schedule.

slots.practicalActivity: Create an Operator with a test email, an Alert tied to a specific error severity that notifies that operator, and a Credential/Proxy pairing that lets an Agent job step run as a different Windows identity (for example for a PowerShell or CmdExec step), then deliberately fail a job step and walk through the Agent error log and job history to triage it.
slots.deliverable: The operator/alert/proxy setup scripts plus a short triage write-up describing where you looked (job history, SQL Server Agent error log) to diagnose the deliberately failed step.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a complete Agent automation package for a test database: a multi-step backup job on a nightly schedule, an alert that emails an operator on failure, and a proxy/credential set up for one step needing elevated OS-level access, then intentionally break one step to confirm the alert fires.
slots.deliverable: The full job/schedule/operator/alert/proxy script plus confirmation (job history or alert history) that the failure alert actually fired.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a linked server from the test instance to a second database (or instance, or a loopback linked server back to itself) using sp_addlinkedserver and sp_addlinkedsrvlogin, then run a 4-part-name query and an OPENQUERY query against it to pull rows from a remote table.
slots.deliverable: The linked-server setup script plus both the 4-part-name query and the OPENQUERY query, each with real returned rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Use SQL Server Configuration Manager to check which protocols (TCP/IP, Named Pipes) are enabled and the TCP port in use, test connectivity with sqlcmd -S <server> and a Test-NetConnection check against that port, then deliberately misconfigure one setting (for example disable TCP/IP) and walk through the resulting error to practice diagnosing it.
slots.deliverable: A connectivity-troubleshooting log: the protocol/port confirmed, the successful sqlcmd connection, and the exact error message from the deliberate misconfiguration plus how to fix it.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine Chapter 8 into a connectivity-check runbook: a linked-server inventory (sys.servers), a working remote-query smoke test, and a protocol/port verification checklist for diagnosing a 'can't connect' ticket.
slots.deliverable: A saved connectivity-runbook covering linked-server inventory, a working remote-query example, and the protocol/port checklist.

slots.practicalActivity: Script a stored procedure and a table definition out of a test database into .sql files and commit them to a local Git repository, simulate a deployment by changing the procedure in a feature branch and merging it, then enable CHANGE_TRACKING on one table to observe what CHANGETABLE(CHANGES ...) reports after an UPDATE.
slots.deliverable: A small Git repo containing the versioned object scripts with at least 2 commits, plus the CHANGETABLE query output showing a tracked change.

slots.practicalActivity: Generate a documentation snapshot of the test database's schema (tables, columns, and foreign keys via sys.tables/sys.columns/sys.foreign_keys), deliberately introduce schema drift by altering a column outside your version-controlled scripts, detect the drift by diffing the current schema against your documented snapshot, then roll back the change using a backup/restore or scripted-rollback approach.
slots.deliverable: The schema-documentation snapshot, a written note describing the drift introduced and how it was detected, and confirmation the rollback restored the original column definition.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a lightweight change-management workflow for the test database: version-controlled object scripts in Git, a documented schema snapshot, and a written rollback plan, then run one complete change through all three steps for a new stored procedure.
slots.deliverable: A short change-management packet: the Git-committed script, the updated schema snapshot, and the rollback plan for that one change.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the triage methodology from the lesson, work through a simulated 'the application is slow' ticket on the test instance: check sys.dm_exec_requests for blocking, check sys.dm_os_wait_stats, check disk/database space, and check Agent job history for a recently failed maintenance job, then draft the escalation message you'd send to a team lead summarizing findings and next steps.
slots.deliverable: A written triage log (what was checked, in order, and what was found at each step) plus the draft escalation/status message.

slots.practicalActivity: Draft a one-page on-call runbook for the test instance covering what to check first for 3 common alert types (disk space, failed backup job, high CPU), then write a full incident report for the simulated incident from the previous slot following a real postmortem structure: timeline, root cause, resolution, and follow-up action items.
slots.deliverable: The on-call runbook (3 alert types with first-response steps) plus a complete incident report with timeline, root cause, resolution, and follow-up items.

slots.practicalActivity: Run a second, different simulated production incident end to end (for example a full transaction log, or an Agent job silently failing for 3 nights) using the triage methodology, on-call runbook, and incident-documentation template built in this chapter, without revisiting the lesson content.
slots.deliverable: A complete incident report for the second scenario, demonstrating the triage-to-documentation workflow applied independently.

slots.practicalActivity: Draft an upgrade plan for taking a test instance from its current build to the latest cumulative update: inventory current version/build with SERVERPROPERTY, check dependent application compatibility level, and write a patching schedule with a maintenance window and communication plan, distinguishing CU/patching from a full version upgrade.
slots.deliverable: A written upgrade/patching plan document covering current state, target state, maintenance window, and rollback trigger criteria.

slots.practicalActivity: Apply a cumulative update (or simulate the step if a real CU isn't available) to a test instance, run a basic post-upgrade validation pass (service starts, SELECT @@VERSION confirms the new build, a few key queries still return expected results), and write a rollback plan specifying exactly what you'd restore from and how you'd confirm the rollback succeeded.
slots.deliverable: A post-upgrade validation checklist with results, plus a written rollback plan naming the specific backup/snapshot it depends on.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine Chapter 11 into a single upgrade-readiness checklist covering planning, patching schedule, validation steps, and rollback plan, then apply it start to finish against the test instance for one real or simulated patch.
slots.deliverable: A completed upgrade-readiness-checklist document with every section filled in with real values from the test instance.

lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: You Inherit a Production Server

slots.practicalActivity: Treat a fresh VM or SQL instance as a production server just inherited with zero documentation: install/configure SQL Server from scratch (service accounts, collation, memory/MAXDOP, file layout) exactly as for a real client, documenting every decision made along the way.
slots.deliverable: A capstone install-and-configure runbook documenting every setup decision, matching the standard used in the Chapter 2 install lab.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same inherited server, build the full security baseline (logins/users/roles, TDE, auditing) and the full maintenance system (Ola Hallengren's scripts wired into Agent jobs), then respond to a simulated production incident using the triage methodology built earlier, end to end.
slots.deliverable: The security-and-maintenance setup scripts plus a complete incident report for the simulated production scenario.

slots.practicalActivity: Run one real change through the full change-management workflow (version-controlled script, schema documentation, deployment, and a rollback plan) against the capstone server, then assemble everything built across the capstone — install runbook, security baseline, maintenance jobs, incident report, and change package — into a single presentation-ready portfolio document.
slots.deliverable: The change-management packet for this scenario plus a capstone portfolio document pulling together every artifact produced across the capstone.

slots.practicalActivity: Present the finished capstone portfolio as if to a hiring manager: walk through the inherited server's install, security, maintenance, one real incident response, and one real change, explaining the reasoning behind each decision out loud (recorded or written as a script) as a mock-interview rehearsal.
slots.deliverable: A recorded or written mock-interview walkthrough script covering all 5 capstone artifacts, plus the final portfolio document ready to share.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can install, configure, secure, and maintain a SQL Server instance from a blank server to production-ready, run day-to-day Agent automation and change management, and handle a production support incident end to end, as demonstrated in a full capstone build on an inherited server.
